record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: Suppose jobs arrive over time to a system with a fixed number n of servers, all jobs share the same concave, sublinear speedup function s(k), and each job's inherent size is unknown at arrival but is drawn from a non-exponential distribution. What server-allocation policy minimizes mean response time in this setting?

evidence.quote: If we consider the same setting as in [34], but where the inherent job size distribution is not exponential, then finding the optimal server allocation policy is an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a queueing system with a fixed number $n$ of identical servers. Jobs arrive over time according to some stochastic arrival process. Each job $j$ has an inherent (sequential) size $X_j$ that is unknown at the time of arrival; the sizes $X_j$ are i.i.d. samples from a known distribution $F$ that is not exponential (and in particular need not be memoryless). All jobs share a common speedup function $s:\{1,2,\dots,n\}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ which is concave and sublinear (i.e., $s(k+1)-s(k)$ is non-increasing in $k$ and $s(k)<k\,s(1)$ for $k\ge 2$). If at a given instant a job is allocated $k$ servers, then it processes its remaining inherent work at rate $s(k)$. Allocations may be changed continuously over time, subject to the constraint that the total number of servers allocated to active jobs is at most $n$ (and jobs may be served in parallel, preempted, and reallocated at no cost). The response time of a job is the time between its arrival and its completion.

Determine the server-allocation policy (a mapping from the system state, namely the set of jobs in the system and their ages, to an allocation of the $n$ servers among them) that minimizes the mean response time in steady state.
artifact.category_tag: Parallel job scheduling in queueing theory
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (2024–2026) have advanced the theory of optimal scheduling for parallelizable jobs with concave speedup functions, including the Consistent Derivative Ratio rule and SmartFill / General Water-Filling algorithms for known sizes, and ServerFilling-Gittins for unknown sizes in related multiserver-job models. However, none of these works appears to give a definitive solution for the specific setting of unknown inherent sizes drawn from a general (non-exponential) distribution with a common concave sublinear speedup on a fixed number of servers. The status thus appears unresolved in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Parallel Scheduling under Concave Speedup Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Prior work assumes job sizes are unknown and drawn from an exponential distribution; this paper studies known sizes with general concave speedups via the CDR rule and SmartFill.
status_evidence.claim: The general non-exponential unknown-size case is not directly resolved; recent progress focuses on known-size or exponential-size settings.

status_evidence.title: On Optimal Server Allocation for Moldable Jobs with Concave Speed-Up
status_evidence.snippet: Optimal server allocation for moldable jobs with concave speed-up functions under stochastic arrivals.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses moldable concave speedup scheduling but under specific distributional assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Scheduling of Parallel Jobs with Unknown Service Requirements
status_evidence.snippet: Studies unknown job sizes with speedup, baseline case with exponential assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: The non-exponential unknown-size variant remains the open question highlighted as future work.
